editor: Various; issued by W. & T. Fordyce
edition: Newcastle upon Tyne: printed and sold by W. & T. Fordyce, No. 15 Grey Street, 1842. Supplied title page, not ebook release year.

deduplication: Deferred to shared integration across next-ten collections and existing corpus; eligibility counts are not admitted counts.
notes: 216 contents entries reconcile to 214 body units: Jenny Hoolet/Lizzie Mudie's Ghost are alternate index titles; Coronation/Invitation index entries refer to one printed song.
Four body h2 headings have page-only index anchors. Explicit mappings preserve all four without treating page breaks as lyric boundaries.
The malformed HTML paragraph around the Coronation Invitation is parsed between literal heading boundaries; all 24 verse lines are retained.

No numerical line cutoff. Three individually reviewed extended narrative/epistolary works are excluded whole; complete performed songs such as Changes on the Tyne and A Voyage to Lunnin remain eligible.

All source spellings, censored names, dialogue wording and abbreviated refrains retained. Typographic markup, page numbers, footnote callouts, prose spoken interludes and editorial notes are recorded as apparatus rather than sung verse. No pronunciation declarations added.
Contents authors retained verbatim; conflicting body bylines explicitly recorded for Canny Sheels and Donocht-Head. No invented full-name expansion.
This screening does not establish exhaustive independent authorship history for anonymous songs; it records the supplied witness and no translation attribution identified.

editorial_exclusions.reason: incomplete_source_work: six-line newspaper quotation in editorial footnote to A Gipsy's Song; not part of the complete body song and not an independently supplied whole poem.
editorial_exclusions.text:
"They brought the piper, Sandy Brown,
Frae Jedburgh to Lochmaben town;
Though whaisling sair and broken down
Auld Sandy seem'd,
His chanter for a pleasing sound
Was still esteem'd."
